description.narrative:
Following the Declaration on ensuring sustainable labour market integration of young people, signed on 8 July 2021 at the second EU-Western Balkans Ministerial Meeting on Employment and Social Affairs (https://www.dei.gov.ba/uploads/documents/bosnia-and-herzegovina-2021-report_1634741127.pdf), the ministers and institutions responsible for employment and labour market governance in Bosnia and Herzegovina have operationalized the Youth Guarantee, an innovative activation scheme targeting young women and men less than 30 years of age and which includes measures spanning across multiple policy areas, such as education, employment, and social protection. In line with the guidance received through the EU’s Economic and Investment Plan, which foresees four stages of implementation of the Youth Guarantee over multiple years, institutions in Bosnia and Herzegovina have reached some of the key milestones foreseen under the first stage, albeit with significant delay due to the country’s complex governance structure. These milestones include: the establishment of a tripartite and multi-ministerial governance structure for the implementation of the Youth Guarantee and the identification of the sub-categories of NEETs to be targeted through the Youth Guarantee (this may change by the end of the year and the reporting should be revisited). Institutions involved in the delivery of the Youth Guarantee have also initiated a multi-year process of levelling up their capacities to implement the Youth Guarantee in line with the principles enshrined in the EU Council Recommendation of 30 October 2020 on A Bridge to Jobs – Reinforcing the Youth Guarantee. In partnership with the European Commission (EC) and the European Training Foundation (ETF), the ILO has set up the EU-ILO Technical Assistance Facility on the Youth Guarantee in the Western Balkans, a demand-driven facility for the provision of high-quality technical assistance to countries implementing the Youth Guarantee. Based on the requests submitted through the Youth Guarantee Coordinator, the ILO has provided support in conducting the statistical mapping of youth not in education, employment, or training (NEET), the review of the policy and legal framework to assess preparedness for the implementation of the Youth Guarantee, the functional assessment of the public employment services and their capacity development requirements in order to function as service delivery mechanism for the Youth Guarantee. Additionally, the ILO has designed and delivered targeted capacity development programmes for the different institutions participating in the operationalization of the Youth Guarantee, including the social partners.
In Bosnia and Herzegovina, the work of state and entity-level institutions in charge of preparing the ground for the youth guarantee relied significantly on the ILO’s facilitation of peer-learning and triangular cooperation with other public employment services from the region and from the EU, via South-South and Triangular Cooperation

description.narrative: In the absence of a national employment strategy for employment several municipalities in Bosnia and Herzegovina have been implementing Local Employment Partnerships (LEPs), an approach whereby local tripartite multi-stakeholder groups devise, through social dialogue and negotiated planning, a coherent set of measures that are tailored to the specific employment challenges in their respective communities and support job creation and transition to formality for those who are most at risk of labour market exclusion. Given the priorities articulated in the entity-level employment strategies, LEPs devote particular attention to the needs of rural communities, where opportunities to access training, business development services and, more generally, decent work are fewer. During the reporting period, 20 LEPs have been implemented, with over 1,200 people (of which 48 per cent were women) having access to training opportunities. Through peer-learning and network meetings, LEPs share experience and develop their capacities towards sustainability. Through the financial contribution of the European Commission, the ILO has provided continuous support to the Local Employment Partnerships (LEPs) in terms of both technical assistance for the design and targeting of relevant measures, and resources for implementation. LEPs have followed the methodology for job creation through placed-based initiative and local employment partnerships articulated by the ILO and already applied in multiple countries across Central and Eastern Europe. The ILO has conducted several capacity development interventions for LEP stakeholders, with particular attention to the needs of social partners and local governance structures that would enable the sustainability of LEPs. Through the ILO, LEPs have had access to the Start and Improve Your Business training package. Additionally, the ILO facilitated mutual and peer-learning activities across LEPs as a means to foster collaboration and sustainability.
